risks.title: Katib emails a case record to an outside address after reading a planted instruction
risks.evidence: Exposure: 120 case files a day, any applicant writes the statement. Controls: none on the recipient. Ease: one sentence. Precedent: Lab 2.2 measured it. Harm: one record with identifier and bank number; recovery needs a breach notice.

risks.title: One hijacked run reads and sends the cases of a whole town
risks.evidence: Exposure: the service account reads every town. Controls: none on search. Ease: two tool calls after a hijack. Precedent: none yet here. Harm: hundreds of records with health notes; not reversible.

risks.title: Mueen shows another applicant's amount or bank number on request
risks.evidence: Exposure: 4,000 conversations a week. Controls: an English phrase filter; the lookup tool takes any identifier. Ease: needs an identifier and a pretext. Harm: one record per request; breach notice.

risks.title: Mueen assures an applicant that the claim will be approved
risks.evidence: Exposure: every conversation about status. Controls: a line in the instructions. Ease: pressing twice. Harm: a wrong personal decision, corrected by the decision letter within weeks.

risks.title: Applicants who write in dialect or in Latin letters get weaker protection and poorer answers
risks.evidence: Exposure: an estimated 15% of messages. Controls: none specific. Precedent: probe rates differ by script in Lab 2.3. Harm: unequal service to a group; trust; needs redesign of filters.

risks.title: Mueen gives a degrading reply about a group of applicants
risks.evidence: Exposure: wide. Controls: instructions and the supplier's safety training. Ease: needs a role-play. Precedent: 1 or 2 in 30 trials. Harm: dignity of the person, public trust, a formal complaint.

risks.title: Case workers send Katib's drafts without reading them
risks.evidence: Exposure: every letter. Controls: a send button after the draft; no sampling. Precedent: median review time 20 seconds in the pilot. Harm: wrong letters reach applicants; corrected on complaint.

risks.title: Applicants learn the fraud-screening rule from Mueen and work around it
risks.evidence: Exposure: needs intent. Controls: the rule sits in the instructions. Ease: works in transliterated Arabic. Harm: some fraud passes screening until the rule changes.

risks.title: The supplier changes the model and behaviour in Arabic shifts unnoticed
risks.evidence: Exposure: every conversation. Controls: a notice clause the supplier interprets. Precedent: one update last year. Harm: quality and refusals change until a retest catches it.

risks.title: Katib drafts a letter with a wrong amount or date
risks.evidence: Exposure: 120 letters a day. Controls: the case worker reads the draft. Precedent: 3% of pilot drafts. Harm: confusion, corrected by a second letter.

risks.title: Drafting skill fades and the Agency depends on one supplier
risks.evidence: Exposure: slow, over years. Controls: none planned. Harm: limited and local at first; slower recovery if the supplier leaves.

risks.title: A planted instruction makes Katib write a false approval note into a case
risks.evidence: Exposure: any statement. Controls: notes are not reviewed. Ease: lower than email, the note must match the form. Harm: a wrong payment decision that needs an audit to find.
